title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.
intro: This training programme equips boards and directors to look beyond structures to how the board really works: the chair, the agenda, the papers, the people around the table and the quality of the decisions they take.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors a practical understanding of the dynamics that decide whether a board challenges management, weighs real alternatives and acts when things go wrong. Participants leave able to improve their agenda, papers and meetings, test the quality of board decisions and see their board the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: How boards work in practice, the role of the chair, agenda and time management, board papers and information quality, information asymmetry and independent assurance, decision quality and looking back, culture, challenge and psychological safety, group think and bias, technical topics and AI in the boardroom, and board evaluation, succession and skills.
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members
Executive directors and senior managers who present to or sit on the board
Company secretaries and heads of governance responsible for board processes and evaluation
Learning Objectives: Explain why sound governance structures do not guarantee effective board behaviour
Evaluate the agenda, board papers and information flows against good practice
Assess the quality of board decisions by their process, not just their outcome
Challenge management effectively while respecting the line between oversight and management
Identify group think, bias and unhelpful dynamics, and apply practical counter-measures
Design a board effectiveness action plan covering evaluation, succession and skills
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two- to three-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with scenarios, exercises and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the board's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)

modules.title: How Boards Really Work
modules.summary: Why a board can have the right composition, committees and terms of reference and still fail to oversee the firm, and what the board's dynamics reveal about its effectiveness.
objectives: Distinguish governance structures from the behaviours that make them work
Explain the board's role in strategy, risk appetite and holding management to account
Identify the common impediments to board effectiveness
syllabus: Form versus substance: what a structural governance review misses
The board's core tasks: direction, oversight and accountability
Common impediments: poor information, weak challenge and ineffective chairing
Seeing your board the way a supervisor does

modules.title: The Chair: Setting the Tone
modules.summary: The chair's pivotal role in creating the conditions for effective challenge and decision-making, and the behaviours that separate an effective chair from an ineffective one.
objectives: Explain the chair's responsibilities for board conduct and performance
Assess chairing behaviours that encourage or suppress contribution
Identify how the chair's relationship with the chief executive shapes the board
syllabus: The chair's role: agenda, discussion, conclusion and board performance
Attributes of an effective chair: authority with humility, patience with incisiveness
Drawing out quieter voices and bringing circular debate to a close
Chair and chief executive: partnership without capture

modules.title: Agenda, Time and Priorities
modules.summary: How expanding board responsibilities collide with fixed meeting time, and how to build an agenda that gives the most important matters the attention they need.
objectives: Recognise the signs of agenda overload and its effect on scrutiny
Apply practical rules for prioritising and sequencing board business
Evaluate the trade-offs in longer, more frequent or larger board meetings
syllabus: Agenda overload: routine reporting crowding out strategy
Sequencing, timing and protecting time for unscheduled discussion
Consent agendas, committees and deciding what not to discuss
Directors' time commitment and the risk of over-boarding

modules.title: Board Papers and Information Quality
modules.summary: What good board information looks like, why more information can mean worse oversight, and how to reshape board packs so that directors can see the issues that matter.
objectives: Define the qualities of good board information
Evaluate board papers for a clear ask, real options and a balanced view of risk
Specify improvements to board packs, presentations and dashboards
syllabus: Good information: accurate, timely, focused, balanced and comparable
Information overload, attention and reliance on mental shortcuts
A good paper: the decision required, options, risks and prior challenge
Presentations, executive summaries and conducting an information audit

modules.title: Information Asymmetry and Independent Assurance
modules.summary: How directors can oversee a business when management always knows more, by understanding how information is produced and drawing on independent sources of assurance.
objectives: Explain the causes and consequences of information asymmetry in the boardroom
Assess the reliance placed on management's own account
Use the control functions, auditors and outside experts to verify what the board is told
syllabus: Why the board always knows less, and what independent directors add
Trusting and verifying: healthy scepticism without hostility
Sources of assurance: risk, compliance, internal and external audit, outside advisers
Side conversations, pre-meetings and the risk of ratification

modules.title: Quality of Decisions and Looking Back
modules.summary: A practical framework for judging how a decision was made rather than how it turned out, and how boards learn by revisiting major decisions and feeding lessons into future practice.
objectives: Apply a structured test to the process behind significant board decisions
Evaluate whether minutes record the rationale for a decision, not just the outcome
Design a routine for revisiting major decisions and learning from them
syllabus: Why, why now, alternatives, assumptions and downside
Success measures and how the board will judge the decision later
Recording rationale and dissent in the minutes
Post-decision reviews and acting on repeat findings

modules.title: Culture, Challenge and Psychological Safety
modules.summary: How boardroom culture shapes the quality of discussion, why effective challenge depends on psychological safety, and how to tell constructive challenge from confrontation.
objectives: Explain how unwritten norms and relationships shape board discussion
Distinguish effective challenge from confrontation and from avoidance
Identify the will, skill and knowledge each director needs to challenge well
syllabus: Boardroom culture: norms, assumptions and the default to collegiality
Psychological safety and the signs of its absence
Effective challenge: evidence-based, focused and persistent
Oversight without micromanagement: where the board's role ends

modules.title: Group Think, Bias and Board Personalities
modules.summary: The cognitive and social traps that undermine board decisions, the board personalities that distort discussion, and practical counter-measures the chair and directors can use.
objectives: Recognise the warning signs of group think and common decision biases
Identify difficult board behaviours and how the chair should respond
Apply practical techniques to counter bias in board decisions
syllabus: Group think, framing, availability and motivated blindness
Decision traps: time pressure, short horizons and isolation
Board personalities: the dominator, the silent director, the absentee and the box-ticker
Counter-measures: devil's advocate, anonymous polling and options before advocacy

modules.title: Technical Topics and AI in the Boardroom
modules.summary: How directors without specialist backgrounds can oversee cyber, technology and other complex risks, and what the use of AI by management and the board means for oversight.
objectives: Assess whether the board has enough knowledge to test technical statements and assumptions
Challenge technical presentations that inform without enabling scrutiny
Evaluate the benefits and risks of AI tools in board preparation and decision-making
syllabus: Cyber, technology and other complex topics: what directors need to understand
Getting the most from technical presentations and specialist advisers
AI-assisted board packs, analysis and preparation: benefits and limits
Accountability for decisions does not move to the tool

modules.title: Keeping the Board Effective
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a board effectiveness action plan covering evaluation, succession, skills, induction and continuing development.
objectives: Evaluate the design of board effectiveness reviews and the follow-through on findings
Use a skills matrix to identify gaps and inform succession and development
Produce a board effectiveness action plan
syllabus: Board evaluation: internal and external reviews, and tracking actions to completion
Succession planning for the chair, independent directors and key executives
Skills matrices, induction and tailored development
Workshop: the board's twelve-month effectiveness action plan

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.

related.title: Induction for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module induction giving new directors of regulated firms the grounding to discharge their duties, understand supervisory expectations and oversee the firm's risks.
